title: Diagnose cafeteria scene and co-located light quality issues
objective: Investigate the reported cafeteria quality failures and produce a concrete remediation plan for a revised SPEAR-ready world and flashlight lighting behavior.
instructions: User feedback: current 500 sqft cafeteria has no windows, no indoor lights, chairs face the wrong way, looks too cartoony, and the co-located light causes the entire room to take on the tint of the object directly in front of the camera.

Inspect the current cafeteria provenance, generator/import artifacts, and relevant flashlight/light control code or docs enough to separate scene-generation issues from renderer/light-transport issues.

Identify likely causes for the room-wide color tint from the co-located light, including Unreal GI/Lumen/indirect light behavior, material albedo/saturation, and flashlight component settings. Recommend the smallest reliable fix or experiment.

Recommend a concrete next build plan for a better cafeteria: windows, indoor fixtures/lights, more realistic materials, correct chair orientation, less cartoony proportions/colors, and validation steps.
constraints: Do not run long-running Blender/Unreal/Infinigen jobs; this is investigation and planning only.
expected_outputs: Root-cause analysis separating scene design/import issues from runtime lighting issues.
Specific build/validation plan with commands or files for Experimenter/Builder to use next.
definition_of_done: Tower can hand off a precise implementation packet to Experimenter and/or Builder without further ambiguity.
